title: सन्नन्तम् — The Desiderative (सन्) Rule Book
subtitle: Compiled from classroom source material on सन्-प्रत्यय (the desiderative affix, 'wants/wishes to do X') and its reduplicated stem-formation pattern
source_note: Compiled from a single classroom source PDF ('07_सन्नन्तम्_-_अभ्यासार्थम्.pdf'), which is itself primarily a drilling/exercise document (अभ्यासार्थम् = 'for practice') built around a smaller set of core rules plus an extensive root-pairing table and several full conjugation tables (contributed by a second author, 'Sundharam C G', for verbs like इत्सति/पिपासति/निगीषति/युयुत्सति/शुश्रूषते/etc.). Only the rule content and a representative sample of the root-pairs are reproduced here; the fill-in-the-blank drills themselves are not. One entry (sannanta-2) corrects an apparent OCR error in the source scan (गम् + सन् was rendered illegibly as 'णिगणिषति'; the standard, well-attested form जिगमिषति is used instead, following the same reduplication pattern -- velar-to-palatal ग→ज -- documented for this root elsewhere). No Aṣṭādhyāyī sūtra numbers are given in the source material for this topic; ashtadhyayi_ref is left null throughout except where a well-known standard citation is added and flagged as such.

sannanta_rules.english_name: Definition: सन् expresses 'wishes/wants to do the root's action'
sannanta_rules.rule: The affix सन्, added to a root, produces a verb meaning 'wishes/desires to [do the root's action]'. सन् is one of twelve related affixes traditionally grouped together as सनादि-प्रत्ययाः (see sannanta-2); सन् itself is the one used for ordinary desiderative formation.

sannanta_rules.english_name: Reference: the twelve सनादि affixes, of which सन् is one
sannanta_rules.rule: Pāṇinian grammar groups twelve affixes together under the technical label सनादि ("सन् etc."): सन्, क्यच्, काम्यच्, क्यङ्, क्यण्, णिङ्, णिच्, यङ्, यक्, आय, ईयङ्, न्तिप्. A root bearing any of these is called सनादि-अन्त (or, when specifically सन् is meant, सन्नन्त). This entry is reference material; only सन् itself is treated in detail in this rulebook.

sannanta_rules.english_name: The desiderative stem is formed by reduplication + weak-grade root + इष्/स् augment
sannanta_rules.rule: The सन्-stem is built by (1) reduplicating the root's initial syllable (with the same general consonant/vowel-selection pattern used in other reduplicating formations -- velars reduplicate as palatals, aspirates deaspirate), (2) keeping the root itself in a weak/unstrengthened grade, and (3) inserting the augment इष् (or, for some roots, स्) before the desiderative's own person-endings. The resulting stem conjugates like a thematic (a-stem) present.

examples.gloss: श्रु root, आत्मनेपदी, root vowel lengthens in reduplicated stem
ज्ञा root, आत्मनेपदी, स्-augment not इष्

sannanta_rules.english_name: The desiderative noun इच्छा ('the wish to X') is formed from the same reduplicated stem
sannanta_rules.rule: Replacing the verbal ending of the सन्-stem with the feminine noun-suffix -आ (rather than a personal verb-ending) produces इच्छा-प्रत्ययान्त, an abstract feminine noun meaning "the wish/desire to [do the root's action]".

examples.gloss: 'the wish to know' -- this word survives in English as 'jijnasa/enquiry'

sannanta_rules.english_name: The desiderative adjective इच्छुः ('desirous of X') is formed from the same reduplicated stem
sannanta_rules.rule: Replacing the verbal ending of the सन्-stem with the u-stem adjectival suffix (उ) instead produces इच्छु-प्रत्ययान्त, an adjective meaning "desirous of [doing the root's action]", declined like a regular u-stem across all three genders.

sannanta_rules.english_name: Caution: the desiderative's object keeps the case the underlying verb's object would take -- NOT the genitive
sannanta_rules.rule: Because इच्छुः/इच्छा look like ordinary nouns/adjectives, learners are tempted to put their object in the genitive (षष्ठी), as one normally would with a noun. This is INCORRECT: the object retains whatever case the underlying (non-desiderative) verb itself would assign to its object -- typically द्वितीया for a transitive root. The source PDF gives this exact अशुद्धम्/शुद्धम् (incorrect/correct) contrast as a caution.
sannanta_rules.process: निषेधः — षष्ठी न भवति; मूलधातोः कर्मविभक्तिः एव अनुवर्तते
sannanta_rules.flagged_nuance: The source explicitly flags this as a common learner error: 'जलस्य पिपासुः' (genitive) is marked अशुद्धम् (incorrect); 'जलं पिपासुः' (accusative, matching पातुम्/पा- root's own object-case) is marked शुद्धम् (correct).

sannanta_rules.english_name: Desiderative pada (voice) generally follows the underlying root's own pada-class
sannanta_rules.rule: Most सन्नन्त verbs conjugate in whichever pada (परस्मैपद or आत्मनेपद) their underlying root normally takes, though some specific roots show a fixed आत्मनेपदी desiderative regardless. The source's conjugation tables illustrate both patterns.
sannanta_rules.book_ref: 07_सन्नन्तम्.pdf (conjugation tables contributed by Sundharam C G)
sannanta_rules.process: प्रायः मूलधातोः पदानुसारेण; केचन धातवः आत्मनेपदिनः एव सन्नन्ते

summary_counts.status: Covers the source PDF's core rule content: definition, the sanadi-list reference, stem formation, the two derived nominal forms (इच्छा/इच्छुः), the genitive-object caution, and pada distribution. Does not reproduce the PDF's extensive practice exercises or its ~25-root pairing table in full (a representative sample is given per rule instead).
